summary: POD GGUF BLOCKER diagnosed (screenshot, live 5090 Pod): ComfyUI-GGUF node import FAILS on the Pod with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gguf'`. TWO gaps: (1) the Pod image's node_lock.json (mpi-ci/cubric-vision-pod/node_lock.json) is a STALE COPY — it does NOT have the ComfyUI-GGUF entry I added to the app's dev_configs/node_lock.json, so the image build never installed the node OR its gguf pip dep (per the bump-rebuild law: node_lock edit = rebuild BOTH images). (2) The per-model VOLUME-install path (routes/remoteModels.js remoteInstallDep, line 284) only passes install_command to the wrapper when dep.installRequirementsCommand (a CUSTOM command) is set — it SILENTLY DROPS installRequirements:true (the standard requirements.txt flag). ComfyUI-GGUF uses installRequirements:true → so even though the wrapper pushed the node folder to the volume, it never ran `pip install -r requirements.txt` → no gguf pkg → import fails. FIX OPTIONS: (a) add ComfyUI-GGUF to the Pod node_lock.json + rebuild the Pod image (bakes node+gguf in, but ComfyUI-GGUF is MODEL-specific not universal — does it belong baked? the image loop installs ALL node_lock nodes regardless of installOnEngine, so adding it there WOULD bake it = acceptable for now); AND/OR (b) FIX remoteModels.js so installRequirements:true also triggers a remote pip install -r requirements.txt (the wrapper must support running requirements.txt for a volume node, not just a custom command) — this is the GENERAL fix so future model-specific nodes with a requirements.txt work remotely. (b) is the real bug. Detail in handoff 60c42614.

Color shift LOCATED (DaVinci): crop-export (our ffmpeg pipeline) == source, NO shift. So ffmpeg/export is clean; extend-from-last-frame drift is NOT export. Shift is DECODE-SIDE ONLY: mediabunny CanvasSink (WebCodecs) renders more vivid than true frame; <video> element is correct. Fix target = make frameSink canvas color-match <video> (range/matrix). Color shift ROOT CAUSE: decoded VideoFrame reports CORRECT color (bt709/bt709/bt709 primaries/transfer/matrix, fullRange:false = limited). Shift is in Chromium drawImage(VideoFrame)->2D-canvas step: it expands limited-range to full-range RGB (sink vivid), while <video>/DaVinci render limited-range as-is (correct). Both technically valid but disagree; <video> is our reference. CanvasSink has NO color option. Fix = correct range in draw. Research agent still finding exact minimal remedy.

Color fix approach: range expansion is INSIDE WebCodecs decode (all 4 draw paths incl copyTo-RGBA give identical vivid pixels; VideoFrame pixels already full-range). Not a draw-trick fix. Simple luma-range compress (219/255) fits R only, not G/B - transform is per-pixel YUV-space, mean-fitting over-corrects. Need proper matrix from research agent. User chose: fix in frameSink. HOLDING for research.

Color fix ANALYSIS: per-channel pixel fit sink->video = R(a0.976,b-2.3) G(a1.016,b-7.4) B(a1.0,b0,resid0). Blue IDENTICAL, R/G diverge by different slopes = YUV MATRIX mismatch (BT.601 vs BT.709), NOT a range op. Confirms research bug 40539111. copyTo-RGBA disproven (same vivid pixels). EXACT fix = self-convert YUV->RGB with correct bt709 limited matrix from copyTo I420 planes. Per-channel RGB approx = resid3/maxDev15 (imperfect). Scope escalation - flagged to user.

CORRECTION to the previous Krea2 entry, caught by the user (disk stayed at 42GB/84% = LTX only, so Krea2 never staged). Krea2 was NOT hot-store staged and was therefore reading from the NETWORK VOLUME, not container disk. Cause found and it is not disk space or eviction: HOT_STORE_MIN_GB = 20 in js/services/commandExecutor.js filters the stage list to weights >= 20GB, and Krea2's largest file is krea2-raw-transformer at 13.49GB - so Krea2 is never even REQUESTED for staging. Consequences: (1) the LTX figures stand as non-volume-I/O (42GB was staged to disk); (2) the Krea2 figures DO include volume reads, so the Pod-vs-local Krea2 comparison is not apples-to-apples - local reads a local SSD while the Pod pulls ~13.5GB over a network volume, which is a strong candidate for the 54s vs 14s cold-penalty gap. ACTIONABLE: the 20GB threshold means our most-used image model gets zero hot-store benefit, ever. But lowering it is not free - CONTAINER_DISK_GB is 50 and LTX High alone occupies 42GB, so staging Krea2 would evict LTX and thrash on every model switch. The threshold and the container disk size have to be sized together.

DECISIVE datapoint 2026-07-23: hot-store staging is NOT the lever, and the earlier 'lower HOT_STORE_MIN_GB' idea is largely DISPROVEN before being built. Attack VRAM load and the per-stage 'prepared for dynamic VRAM loading' re-prep instead.

note: Root cause found by code read (no repro needed): MpiBaseApp binds Hotkeys generation.run at SETUP, but closing an app only HIDES its overlay - the shell destroys the instance only when a DIFFERENT app opens. So the closed Head Swap app kept a live Ctrl+Enter handler; the next Ctrl+Enter in the main workspace fired BOTH the PromptBox run and the stale app _run, enqueuing a second job from the still-persisted s_appInputs. FIXED. Root cause: MpiBaseApp binds the global generation.run hotkey at setup, but closing an app only HID the overlay - the shell destroyed the instance only when a DIFFERENT app opened. HotkeyManager fires ALL handlers bound to an id, so the next Ctrl+Enter ran the PromptBox run AND the closed app _run, re-submitting the persisted s_appInputs. Explains every observation (same params, real prompt id, injector logged 8.5 min later = the phantom dispatched when the 1m41s Qwen edit drained the single remote lane). Fix: the app emits close outward and the shell DESTROYS the instance on it (every open remounts fresh), killing all stale listeners. Proven live on the real Electron shell by tests/desktop/app-close-destroys-instance.spec.js - passes with the fix, FAILS (Expected 0, Received 1) with both source files stashed. Blast radius swept: all 30 Hotkeys.bind sites; MpiBaseApp was the only hidden-but-alive holder of a global hotkey. Real bug was that tile mode was one-way - once _tileMode was set, step() only moved _percent and never advanced _stage, so the refiner's bar was swallowed and the fill ran 0-100 percent a second time while the readout sat on the last tile (reads as a stall at the end of every upscale). Rejected the simpler '_total = tiles + 1': it fixes the printed total but not the stall, and tile() is shared by all 9 USDU cards - the 7 without a refiner would advertise a stage that never runs. Fix counts inner bars since the last tile bar; USDU emits its tile bar before every tile's inner bar, so during tiling the counter resets each tile and only a post-tile pass reaches 2. On the second bar it leaves tile mode and falls through to the normal per-bar logic, which stages it and self-corrects the total. 1 tile -> 2/2, 4 tiles -> 5/5. tile() untouched, so tile counting is unchanged. Ceiling named in the comment: assumes one inner bar per tile, true while all 9 USDU cards run seam_fix_mode None (swept). Guarded by tests/tile-post-pass-stage.test.cjs, 5 cases, negative-control proven (3 of 5 fail against the unfixed module, 5/5 pass restored). eslint clean. Still NOT verified in the app.

Live app test caught a hole in the first progress fix. routes/comfy.js forwards the RAW tqdm value from 'USDU: t/T', so T tiles emit T+1 events (0/T .. T/T) - the last fires AFTER the final tile's inner bar. The first cut re-armed the post-tile detector on EVERY tile bar, so that trailing tick re-armed it after the last tile and the refiner never tripped it; app still read 1/1 on both stages. Guard is now 'if (tileIndex < tiles)' - arm only for a tile that will actually run. The original test called tile() once per tile and never modelled the trailing tick, so it passed against broken code: a WRONG test, not a thin one. It now models the tick explicitly. Also added the user's requested honest total: progressStages.js records 'krea2_upscaler.json': {postTile: 1} (no 'single' - the tile count is a runtime value that tile mode overrides), new postTileBarsFor() shares _baseKey with stagesFor, commandExecutor passes it into createStageProgress, and tile() uses _total = _tileOffset + tiles + _postTileBars. A blanket +1 in tile() was rejected because 7 of the 9 USDU cards have no refiner and would advertise a stage that never runs. Stage clamp in tile() also had to move from min(_total, ...) to min(_tileOffset + tiles, ...) or the trailing tick advances into the refiner slot early. Now: grid off 1/2 -> 2/2; grid on 4 tiles 1/5..4/5 -> 5/5; other upscalers unchanged. Test at 6 cases, all pass; TWO negative controls - vs unfixed HEAD 5 of 6 fail, vs the first cut 4 of 6 fail including both trailing-tick cases. eslint clean on all three touched modules. Verified: postTileBarsFor returns 1 for both krea2 upscaler variants and 0 for chroma/sdxl/pony/ill, stagesFor unregressed (krea2_t2i 2, ltx_t2v 3). Awaiting user re-test in the app.

Upscale op applies the factor TWICE - 1.5x on a 768x1344 source yields 1728x3024 (2.25x). Root is NOT the factor and NOT the workflow: Input_Upscale_Factor has exactly one writer (PromptBoxControls.upscaleFactor, injects the raw 1.5), the sidecars for upscale_013/014/015/016 all record 1.5, node 1657 feeds only MpiGridDimensions.upscale_factor and UltimateSDUpscale.upscale_by, and the user ran the same graph in the ComfyUI browser and got the correct size. The graph is fed the WRONG IMAGE: generationSettings.mediaItems points at Media/.preview-assets/1ed8902c...png which measures 1152x2016, i.e. the 768x1344 source already enlarged 1.5x. 1152x2016 * 1.5 = 1728x3024 exactly. t2i_039's own sidecar reports pixelDimensions 768x1344 and has no previewAssets, so that file is not a full-res twin - it exists only in the content-addressed staging store. All four runs used the same hash, consistent with a deterministic pre-scale of the same source at the same factor. UNPROVEN: which code writes the pre-scaled staged copy. Start there.

User-reported context added, and it shifts the leading hypothesis. At the time of these runs the user (1) DELETED several upscale entries to make room to keep testing, and (2) at one point had a generation finishing in the ComfyUI browser while starting another in the app. (1) lines up with the MPI-225 comment above _opScopedMediaItems in generationService.js: a stale PromptBox media chip gets snapshotted into generationSettings.mediaItems and injects the wrong image, and the reference orphans once a card in that lineage is deleted. _opScopedMediaItems only filters chips whose mediaType the op does not declare - upscale DOES declare an image slot, so a stale image chip passes straight through and becomes Input_Image. That explains all four runs recording the same asset hash with a correct factor and a correct graph. (2) is unlikely alone: a one-off race would not produce the SAME hash at dispatch on four consecutive runs, so treat it as a possible aggravator. The earlier deliberate-pre-scale guess is SUPERSEDED - no code was found doing it and the stale-chip path explains the data without it; do not start from it. Found live 2026-07-29 while validating MPI-394 on a fresh CPU Pod: the user pressed Install on SDXL NSFW and the tile sat on 'Queued...' with nothing else installing. Proven from the live app: /comfy/downloads/status held NO sdxl-nsfw job at all (only engine:assets and klein-4b, both complete) and /comfy/downloads/active returned {models:[],engine:false} - so the POST never fired. Installs are serialised through a client-side promise chain gated on _inFlight (downloadService.js:76, MPI-184); 'queued' is only set when _inFlight > 0, so something held the chain. The only other start() in the session was engine:assets (drift heal logged nothing, no generation ran, App Library never opened) - so its chain link had not settled DESPITE download:complete having fired, which the completion toast proves. That is only possible if the listener was armed after the event. Root: run() armed _awaitDownloadDone INSIDE the post-POST .then(), but routes/downloadManager.js calls _startPendingDeps() BEFORE res.json() (register-before-respond, G8) and a fully-satisfied install goes terminal right there - 0 queued deps, nothing to download. The terminal broadcast therefore beats a listener armed after await res.json(). _awaitDownloadDone then burns its full 30-MINUTE ceiling with _inFlight pinned at 1, and every install clicked in that window sits at 'queued' forever - with no revert timer, because downloadService.js:90 arms one only for 'pending'. SHIPS TO USERS: _installRemoteEngineAssets re-runs on the first connect of EVERY session and is a pure no-op once the volume already holds the weights, so the common case (any session after the first) is the one that wedges, and the victim is the first model install after connecting to a Pod. NOT caused by the earlier volume-full session; a fresh volume would HIDE it, because a real 1.76GB download always lands after the listener is armed. Second, cosmetic half of the same trigger: notificationService announced 'engine:assets installed.' - a raw internal job id - as a toast and, unfocused, an OS notification, on every connect, even though shell.js states the heal must run silently.

Structural finding, now in docs/workflow-authoring/mpi-nodes.md: ExecutionBlocker only travels downstream and an OUTPUT_NODE is always executed, so gating after a sampler never stopped the sampler - which is why the wan22 _stage2 twins exist with Stage1_Bypass deleted. Both forcing paths are now fixable with lazy gates, so those twins can likely go (LTX six differ by ONE baked boolean). H3 cannot produce whole seconds: n%17==5 at 24 fps means 2 s is really 2.33 s (56 frames, measured on a real mp4); 8 s is the shortest exact one. H3 does not repeat frames (56 decoded, 56 unique), so the WAN/LTX remove-frame node is unnecessary. App seek needs no change - MpiVideoControlBar derives effFps from frameCount/duration. OPEN RISK: every measurement on this card ran at 56 frames and the trained range is 124-362, so the 5-step preview floor, the pruned/unpruned A/B and the timing table are all provisional - re-run at 124 before they become tier defaults. Pruned vs unpruned RE-CONFIRMED by the user at higher canvases (480x864 and 768x1344, 56 frames, seed 4, 20 steps, same prompt and source, only unet_name varied). Spatial quality EQUAL at both - confirms the 2026-08-05 call at a 2.7x larger canvas. NEW FINDING: the difference is TEMPORAL, not spatial - unpruned is slightly more expressive in facial motion (wider smile, more eye crinkle) on the same seed; pruned is more restrained. User judged it not worth 13 GB. Decision stands, ship pruned, but the REASON is narrower than it looked: speed is dead as an argument (pruned was 23.8 s faster at 768x1344 but 4.6 s SLOWER at 480x864 - the sign flips and both sit inside the ~25 s run-to-run spread), and resident memory was already dead since 2026-08-05 (ComfyUI streams per layer, footprint capped by what fits not by file size). The only real argument left is DOWNLOAD SIZE, 20.97 GB vs 34.04 GB, which for a shipped product is decisive on its own. CAVEAT carried into section 9: the expressiveness gap was seen at 56 frames, under half the trained minimum, and a temporal signature is exactly what would compound over 124-362 frames - so the row is cleared for spatial quality and STILL OPEN for motion at length. Also recorded in section 5b: (1) MINIMAX_H3_RATIOS is one tier SHORT by this repo own convention - ratios.js:56-58 already ships WAN an above-native very_high at 1920x1088 called an extrapolated detail tier, and H3 would extrapolate LESS (1.43x vs WAN 1.50x), both /32-clean; the template Note: Size Settings Reference reaching 2.0 MP is NOT evidence, it is the generic ResolutionSelector column byte-identical across all three templates. (2) Resolution trades texture for cleanliness - higher canvas means less noise and less morphing but plastic skin, because more latent cells let the model render its own clean-skin prior; the texture at 480x864 is capacity-limited decode texture, NOT retained source grain (same source across both canvases, and high-frequency is stripped by lanczos + the /16 encode before the model sees it). Product consequence: grain belongs in a post pass, not in a tier choice.

(1) PATCHED, a money leak: the GPU Pod was created with a bare /remote/pod/create + a hard 20-minute waitReady, and die() is process.exit(1) which deletes NOTHING. A dead host would have cost 20 idle minutes and then LEAKED a rented GPU Pod, billing until a human noticed. Also found: an in-flight huggingface install does not touch the volume at all (49,664 bytes used with 1.27GB fetched, jumping to 26.37GB on completion), which may undercut the card's premise that a partial inflates du - resolve that before calling the fix right. That demotes FIX 2 - whatever holds the box at 42 percent survives every app exiting, so it is a service or the kernel, not watchers. Supporting idle evidence: no readable process is a resident hog (msedge 0.97 percent avg, Code 1.09, engine python 1.47), box totals 4.53 percent with privileged 2.4 and DPC 0.15, and Defender is NOT mid-scan (ScanInProgress empty, FullScanAge 510 days). Fixed and verified. Clip playback was a one-shot latch on the gallery card element, armed by the single VHS_latentpreview marker a burst previewer sends once per sampler run - so a missed marker stranded the whole run in still mode, which is a whole clip flashed per step at burst speed. It read as single-pass-only because a multi-stage H3 run is two prompts and gets a second arming. Clip state now lives on the generation (activeGenerations, dropped with the gen) and rides every frame to the card, which mirrors instead of latching, so a miss self-heals on the next frame. The marker's {length, rate} were also being discarded outright by commandExecutor: playback now runs at the announced rate (H3 24, LTX 16 - 8fps was a hardcode) and the ring is sized by the announced length (48 was clipping H3's 56-frame clip down to its tail). BREAKTHROUGH, judged by Fabio: appi2v_512_00001.mp4 has GOOD LIP SYNC from a supplied audio track, on ltx_i2v_t2v_template.json exactly as it ships - no lipdub IC-LoRA, no talking-head LoRA, no new node. That closes the singing case and confirms the reframe that the capability already ships and the gap is a video input. Two conditions had to be met, both missing from the earlier appi2v_lipsync attempt that read as a failure: the prompt must carry the spoken line (adding it moved the output by PSNR y 20.41 on a fixed seed, against 44.31 for an identical generation), and Input_Height must be divisible by 64 - the graph halves it at #156 MpiMath floor(a/2) and the latent then floors to a multiple of 32, so 544 became 512 while ImageResizeKJv2 sized the conditioning image to the injected 544, leaving the image 32px taller than the latent it conditioned. The 'different woman' complaint was neither of these: frame 0 of lipdub_face.mp4 is the BACK OF HER HEAD, so the model was handed no face and invented one, and faithfully continued the turn - diagnosed by looking at the frame rather than trusting the earlier session's label. The start frame must SHOW the face, which extends the face-size finding. On Fabio's question about elix3r/LTX-2.3-22b-AV-LoRA-talking-head: never tried, and not what this needs - it is a 428MB subject LoRA for one identity (trigger OHWXPERSON, 26 clips), a different file from the 1.16GB ltx-2.3-id-lora-talkvid-3k on disk, its lips follow GENERATED audio so it does not serve the singing case, and its licence forbids commercial use. Its README is valuable though: their training clips are made with BASE LTX-2.3 and no LoRA via LTX-2-3-I2V-Custom-Audio.json, whose audio path is identical to ours, and it documents 1280x704 @ 25fps for image+audio, a mouth-behaviour prompt block, and that simple dark backgrounds improve lip sync.

HEAD BRANCH REVISED (Fabio): stage 1 is UNCHANGED and still required - face_yolov8n plus the ordered filter still SELECT which head is operated on, and that picked region is the area to inpaint - but the mask that gets filled is a UNION OF THREE SAM3 SEMANTIC MASKS, hair + face + hat. Reasons from experience: a face-only mask fails on a hatted character (measured on the cowboy-movie work, where inpainting a face under a hat required the hat in the mask), hair falling over clothing needs a precise hair mask, and a box stamped on the head makes the inpaint model destroy the clothing detail it covers and invent new detail in its place. The `paint` step kind is BUILT and proven live - the app half is unblocked. MpiStepPaint mounts PaintManager + brushDab.js (the History paint tool's own layer and dab, no second brush) on a plain canvas stage, the same relationship MpiStepCrop has with CropManager, and binds through STEP_MEDIA returning the layer ALONE as an RGBA PNG at the SOURCE's natural size - not the layer's own working size, which is what would silently misplace the object on a photo over PAINT_MAX_EDGE 4096. Every mutation records into its own UndoStack per docs/masking-undo.md. ONE frame change was unavoidable and no handoff had seen it: the merged graph takes TWO images (Input_Image AND Input_Paint) while _deriveRunMedia could only REPLACE a role's media, so a paint step would have eaten the photo - a step may now declare `mediaRole` and the frame appends when that role is empty; omit it and crop's behaviour is byte-identical. Verified live in an isolated instance on :58669 (never the user's port): layer back at the source's 1200x800, undo restores a stroke to the pixel (19529 -> 32893 -> 19529), Clear and undo-after-Clear hold, the eraser's undo restores 25274 exactly, wheel sizing clamps 2..400, a fresh mount seeded with the value restores the identical drawing (Reuse), and an unpainted step reports null and derives no file. That last one leaves ONE obligation on the WIRING, silent when got wrong: with no drawing there is no Input_Paint file and MpiLoadImageFromPath runs on its baked authoring path, returning a confident wrong result. The frame cannot guard it - a null from STEP_MEDIA legitimately means 'nothing changed' for crop. Contract: docs/playbooks/add-flow/ui/paint-gizmo.md.

Open question 1 ANSWERED in code, and the answer removes the cross-step dependency entirely. The ratio must be a field on the PAINT STEP ITSELF, not a ratio step and not a flow-level field: a gizmo step's own declared fields seed into _stepValues[role].fields at SETUP (MpiBaseFlow.js:381-393) and that object is handed to the gizmo as props.value at mount, so the ratio is readable before the first _report() with zero frame plumbing; the frame ALSO already calls el.onField(id,val) on a step-field change (MpiBaseFlow.js:1326) with a comment naming 'a ratio lock' as the use case. A flow-level field would NOT be readable - mount props are {media,step,value,onChange} and _fieldValues is not among them. No new field type needed either: declaredFields.js supports select and radio. Zero-media flows already work end to end - character-sheet has no inputSchema and step 0 renders 'This flow needs no input media.' THREE frame/gizmo touch points remain, all small: (1) MpiBaseFlow.js:1284 _buildStepSlide refuses to mount a gizmo when _mediaForRole(role) is null, printing 'Add the image for this step on the first step.'; (2) MpiBaseFlow.js:2211 _deriveRunMedia does 'if (!media) continue', so with nothing uploaded the painted layer never becomes media at all - this is the second half of the same blocker and is easy to miss; (3) MpiStepPaint.js:588 holds ALL init (_natural, paint.init, undo.clear, _syncCanvasSize, _refit, restore, _draw, _report) inside the imgEl load handler, which never fires with no url - extract it to _initSurface(w,h) and call it directly from the ratio. That extraction is exactly what kills the brief's silent 1x1 PNG trap.

block_if_empty OFF on Input_Image - Fabio's call, and it is correct; my objection was wrong and is retracted. I warned that img.py:396 returns a 1x1 BLACK image with width/height 0, recreating the silent 1x1 trap in the graph. I had missed that the 1x1 goes straight through Scale Image to Total Pixels. Verified in the engine source (comfy_extras/nodes_post_processing.py:247): total = megapixels*1024*1024 = 1048576, scale_by = sqrt(1048576/1) = 1024, and with his resolution_steps 16 the result is round(1*1024/16)*16 = 1024. So an empty path normalises to exactly 1024x1024 on a multiple of 16. GetImageSize reads the SCALED image, so the loader's 0,0 width/height outputs are never consumed. torch.zeros is BLACK, which is the correct neutral for both surviving arms - scribble and canny both encode strokes as white-on-black, so a uniform black hint reads as 'no strokes' and ControlNet contributes nothing. Net behaviour with nothing supplied: a plain 1024x1024 txt2img, which is a better product outcome than an ExecutionBlocker returning no output at all.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED - the canvas-size picker moved but the canvas stayed square, and it was MY bug. el.onField called _blankSize(), which re-reads props.value?.fields?.canvasSize. props.value is the object captured in the closure AT MOUNT, and the frame writes a field by REPLACING the step's value object (_writeDeclaredField: _stepValues[role] = { ...prev, fields: {...} }), so the captured object keeps the ORIGINAL size forever. The control moved, nothing else did, and nothing errored. FIX: take the new value from the argument the frame already passes - el.onField(fieldId, val) - and parse THAT. Split _parseSize(raw) out so mount-time (_blankSize off props.value, correct there) and change-time (off val) share one parser. Generalises: a gizmo must never re-read props.value to learn about a change, because the frame hands it a new object rather than mutating the old one.

DROPDOWN TRUNCATION ROOT CAUSE, and it is a Primitive bug that predates this flow: MpiDropdown.js positionList() did `list.style.width = rect.width + 'px'`, pinning the portalled menu to the TRIGGER's width. A trigger narrower than its own longest option therefore ellipsised every option (.mpi-dropdown__option gets text-overflow: ellipsis), so the user picked between 'Squa...' and 'Land...'. FIX: the trigger width becomes a FLOOR - minWidth = rect.width with width: max-content - plus a max-width: min(420px, 100vw - 16px) in the stylesheet so a long option cannot open a window-wide menu, plus an overhang correction on `left` so a right-hand control no longer opens past the viewport edge now that the menu may exceed its trigger. Swept as a shared primitive: this only ever REVEALS text that was hidden, never narrows a menu, and the desktop specs that exercise MpiDropdown (model-settings-popup, popup-contract) stay green.

THE RESHAPE NOW CARRIES THE DRAWING - the refuse-when-drawn guard is REMOVED, and Fabio's reaction is why. He said he had not tested changing the canvas size because he was 'afraid I might lose my beautiful drawing'. The drawing was in fact safe (el.onField bailed on !paint.isEmpty()), but a control that moves and does nothing is worse than either real behaviour: he would not touch it at all rather than risk a picture he had just spent real time on. Fixed properly instead of documented: on a size change the layer is CONTAIN-FIT into the new canvas and restored. New helper _refitLayer(url, from, to) pre-renders into the destination size, and that pre-render is load-bearing rather than tidy - PaintManager.setFromDataURL does drawImage(img, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height), so handing it a square layer for a wide canvas would STRETCH the drawing rather than place it. Contain, centred, never crop: the user drew a whole picture and changing the page shape must not decide which part to discard. _initSurface(w, h, restoreUrl = seeded.paint) now takes what to restore, so mount-time seeding and reshape-time carrying share one path.

SECOND BUG FIXED IN THE SAME EDIT, and it would have silently distorted every reshaped drawing. _layerUrl() memoises the exported PNG behind _urlDirty and only 'the four real mutations' set that flag - a reshape was not one of them. So after a resize the memo still held the layer at the OLD size while _natural reported the NEW one, and composePaintComposite draws the layer across the full w x h: a square layer stretched into a wide frame, no error, no warning. _initSurface now sets _urlDirty = true unconditionally. Cost is one extra encode at mount. PROVEN by the layer coming back at 1344x768 after the reshape rather than the stale 1024x1024.

ponytail ceiling recorded in the code: the reshape itself is not undoable, because undo.clear() is part of arming a surface. Reaching for a size and reaching back costs one contain-fit round trip, so square -> wide -> square leaves the drawing smaller than it started. Record the reshape as a real undo entry if anyone bounces between shapes often enough to notice.

CONTAIN-FIT ON RESHAPE WAS WRONG AND IS REPLACED BY A 1:1 RE-CANVAS. Fabio hit it on his SECOND reshape: square -> portrait gave white spacing on top, portrait -> square came back with the drawing visibly smaller and margin on all four sides, and he called it - 'it's most likely going to keep adding spacing if we go down that route'. Correct: each reshape contain-fit the ALREADY-FITTED result, so the drawing shrank and gained margin every single time. I had written that up as an accepted ponytail ceiling ('square -> wide -> square leaves the drawing smaller than it started'); hitting it on the second interaction means it was never an acceptable ceiling, it was a bug. The deeper error was scaling at all. The control is called CANVAS SIZE, so it changes the PAGE the drawing sits on - exactly what an image editor's canvas-size command does - and never resizes the artwork. _refitLayer is now _recanvasLayer: draw at 1:1, centred, transparent where the page grew, cropped where it shrank. Simpler than the scaling version too (no scale maths).

THE MASTER LAYER is what makes the round trip lossless, and without it the re-canvas would erode the drawing just as badly in the other direction. Re-canvassing CROPS whichever axis shrank, so feeding the next reshape the cropped result would lose those pixels permanently. New `_master` holds the layer as last DRAWN, never as last reshaped, and every re-canvas works from it. Refreshed only when the user has actually drawn since it was taken, detected via `_urlDirty` - which is a valid signal precisely because _report() clears that flag at the end of every reshape, so a true reading means real strokes rather than the reshape's own re-encode. Seeded lazily, so the reuse path (mount with value.paint, then reshape) is covered by the same branch.

PROVEN LOSSLESS with pixel measurements on the seeded-layer path. Baseline: a 200x200 mark at (100,100) in a 1024x1024 layer reads bbox [100,100,298,298], 198x198 at the 2px sampling step. SQUARE -> PORTRAIT (896x1152): bbox [36,164,234,362], mark still 198x198 - matching the hand-computed 1:1 centred offsets exactly (x -64, y +64) and confirming no scaling. PORTRAIT -> SQUARE: bbox [100,100,298,298], 198x198 - IDENTICAL to baseline. Then a five-reshape chain 1344x768 -> 768x1344 -> 1152x896 -> 896x1152 -> 1024x1024 returned [100,100,298,298] with lossless true. The 1344x768 step reads 198x170 because the mark's top 28px goes off-canvas - the crop a canvas resize SHOULD do - and it returns to 198x198 on the next reshape, which is the master proving the crop is display-only and not destructive. npm test 738/738 after the change.

THE SKIPPED STEP WAS A SPARSE-ARRAY HOLE, and the root is one character. `_mediaGroups[].items` is SPARSE BY CONTRACT - clearing a slot `delete`s its index rather than splicing, so later images keep the role their slot names, and the code says so ('a hole means that slot is empty, which is legal'). But `Array.prototype.find` is one of the few iterators that does NOT skip holes: it calls back with `undefined`. `_mediaForRole` used a bare `it.role`, so the first navigation after clearing a filled slot threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'role')`. Fixed to `it?.role`. The `delete` is CORRECT and was left alone - splicing would silently shift every later image into another slot's role, which is a worse bug than the one being fixed. Swept every other reader of `items` in the file: line 828 uses index access (a hole reads undefined, falsy, fine), 2099 uses `.filter(Boolean)` (filter skips holes), 736/851 are direct writes. 558 was the only hole-intolerant one.

WHY THIS BUG WAS INVISIBLE IN EVERY CHANNEL THAT NORMALLY CATCHES ONE, worth keeping because the symptom pointed at the wrong subsystem for four wrong hypotheses. The TypeError fired inside `_renderSlide` BEFORE `slidesEl.innerHTML = ''`, so the DOM never swapped while `_current` had ALREADY been advanced by `_goTo`. Result: press Next once and nothing appears to happen; press again and it lands on Generate, which builds no gizmo and never calls `_mediaForRole`. It reads exactly like 'the flow skips the middle step', which is how Fabio reported it, and it sent me looking at `_getSteps`, `_syncChrome`, `_lastIndex` and `STEP_KINDS` - all of which are static and all of which were fine. It was an UNCAUGHT renderer TypeError, so nothing reached `clientLogger` and app.log showed a clean session; and the node suite cannot reach it because the bug only exists once a slot has really been filled and then cleared. What finally found it was reproducing in an isolated instance and reading the CONSOLE, not the log. Fabio's own detail - 'first press stays, second takes me to the last stage' - is the signature of a throw between the index write and the DOM swap; treat that shape as diagnostic.

SECOND BUG IN THE SAME HANDLER: clearing a slot THREW AWAY THE USER'S TYPED PROMPT. `delete _stepValues[freedRole]` was justified as 'a removed image invalidates the step bound to that role', which is right about the DRAWING - those strokes were placed over the image that just left - and wrong about everything else in that record. A gizmo step's DECLARED FIELD VALUES live in `_stepValues[role].fields`, and for Scribble that is both `canvasSize` AND `positive`, the user's own words. So removing an upload silently discarded a typed prompt and reset the canvas size to Square. Now the record is rebuilt as `{ fields }` - the paint layer and brush state go, the declared fields stay. Found by reading, not reported: Fabio only noticed the canvas-size half.

PROVEN BY REPRODUCTION, BEFORE AND AFTER, in an isolated instance (own port 60689, own profile) rather than by argument. BEFORE: seed a filled slot, click clear, press Next - console carries `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'role')` with the full stack `_mediaForRole:558 -> _buildStepSlide:1284 -> _renderSlide:1492 -> _goTo:1511`, and the ticker stays on index 0. AFTER: start 0, clear, still 0, Next -> index 1 WITH a mounted canvas (so it is the real gizmo, not the 'add an image' placeholder), Next -> index 2, and zero console errors. New regression spec tests/desktop/flow-clear-slot-advances.spec.js drives that exact sequence and asserts the middle index plus an empty console - a node test cannot see this, and no log line exists to assert on. Suites: npm test 737/738 (the one failure is the unrelated orphan-sweep isolation leak), npm run test:desktop 27/27, eslint clean. No mutation test was run to prove the spec fails without the fix: the pre-fix stack trace is that evidence already, and a mutation run that dies mid-way leaves a real source file broken on disk.

STILL OPEN AND IT IS A UX CALL, NOT A BUG: the canvas-size picker is inert when an image is uploaded. `_hasMedia` is a `const` captured at mount and `onField` bails on it (`if (fieldId !== 'canvasSize' || _hasMedia) return`). That is BY DESIGN - the FlowDef predicted it in a comment ('it renders even when the user HAS uploaded a drawing, because the frame has no conditional-field support ... answered with copy rather than a showWhen, a real feature with real blast radius for one control'). Fabio hit it and reported it, which is the same shape as the reshape guard he rejected earlier: 'a control that moves and does nothing is worse than either real behaviour'. Three ways out, and it is his pick: hide the field when a slot is filled (needs `showWhen` in the field vocabulary), disable it with a reason on the control, or make it WORK by re-canvassing the uploaded image the same 1:1 centred way `_recanvasLayer` already re-canvasses the paint layer - which is coherent with the semantic already settled here, that canvas size changes the PAGE and never the artwork. NOT actioned without his call.

CANVAS SIZE IS NOW DISABLED WHEN THE SLOT IS FILLED - Fabio picked option 2 of three (hide / disable / make it work). New STEP-FIELD flag `blankOnly: true`, resolved in `_buildFieldsRow` against `_mediaForRole(step.role)` and passed down as `disabled`. Chosen over a general `showWhen` predicate deliberately: one boolean with one meaning, against a expression language the frame would then own forever for a single control. The FlowDef's old note ('Only used for a blank canvas') was fine print under a live control; reworded to 'Sets the size of a blank canvas. A drawing you add keeps its own size.' so that on a DISABLED control it reads as the reason rather than as a caveat. `MpiStepPaint.onField`'s own `_hasMedia` bail is KEPT as defence in depth - the gizmo should refuse a change it cannot honour even if a future caller forgets the flag.

`disabled` is honoured on the `select` branch of declaredFields.js ONLY, and that is a recorded ceiling rather than an oversight. HERO REBUILT AS A TWO-STAGE DISSOLVE - Fabio rejected the seam wipe: 'I don't like how the graphic is in the first stage.' He is right about why: a half-drawing/half-render first frame reads as TWO PICTURES GLUED TOGETHER, where a dissolve reads as one picture becoming itself. The drawing now lies ON the render and lifts in two stages, because the drawing IS two things - the white GROUND fades first, so the finished picture appears behind the strokes and the drawn lines are briefly readable on it, and then the STROKES lift too. A PAINT-GIZMO DRAWING IS NOT INK ON TRANSPARENCY, and that measurement is what made the tile work. A blank canvas is painted WHITE, so imported_002.png is RGBA but 100% OPAQUE (measured), with 45.5% of its pixels saturated strokes. 'Keep its own alpha' is therefore a no-op - my first 'ink only' attempt changed nothing - and ghosting the flat sketch over the render washes the whole picture pale, which reads hazy rather than 'a drawing on a picture'. ANIMATING AN OVERLAY'S OPACITY IN THIS FFMPEG BUILD HAS EXACTLY ONE WORKING FORM, after three dead ends that all look reasonable: `colorchannelmixer=aa` and `blend`'s opacity take a STATIC value; chaining fade=out then fade=in on one stream makes the two fight over the same alpha (the in-fade zeroes everything before its st); and a separate gray mask + alphamerge needs the plate TWICE, but a filter label can only be CONSUMED ONCE - and `split` to get it twice walks into the gray-negotiation trap that drains the plate's colour. What works: `format=rgba,geq=r='r(X,Y)':g='g(X,Y)':b='b(X,Y)':a='alpha(X,Y)*(RAMP)'` with RAMP a 0-1 if(lt(T,...)) chain. DESIGN REDECIDED by Fabio, and first live finding. Design: stage 1 takes target + object; stage 2 is a real transform gizmo (place/scale/rotate, the History Place tool's own ShapeManager 'place' mode) that STAMPS the object onto the target; the edit model then gets the stamped composite and is told to make it real. The stamp is CONDITIONING, not output - which is why this is NOT the paste architecture MPI-621 disproved (there the paste was the final placement with only cosmetic repair, so it could never occlude; here the model re-renders the region and can put foreground over the object). It also collapses the precision worry: the model repairs rather than invents. Topology is Draw It In's 35 nodes unchanged, with 'the drawing' swapped for 'the placed object'. Agreed ladder, one question per rung: (1) stamped composite alone, (2) + clean object as Input_Image_2 if fine detail drifts, (3) + original as Input_Image_3. App ALREADY wires all three (kleinEdit mediaInputs, 2/3 optional), so every rung is testable with no build - Fabio is testing prompts in the app now. FINDING 1 (live, first plate): BiRefNet is SALIENCE segmentation, not SEMANTIC - on a gun-and-knife-on-cloth source it returned all three, because they are one foreground arrangement. Not a threshold or model-quality problem. Fix Fabio specified: stage 2 carries a Remove Background button PLUS an erase/restore brush, so the model does the precise part (it nailed the gun's silhouette) and the human does the semantic part (wiping two big leftover blobs, which needs no precision). Design rule: keep bgMask and userMask as TWO layers composited at dispatch, never flattened, or toggling Remove Background destroys the user's erasures; and the brush must work with the toggle OFF too, for sources BiRefNet whiffs entirely. This grows stage 2 beyond the 'one component, one line' estimate - it is place gizmo + bg toggle + add/subtract alpha brush + UndoStack - but every piece already exists and it still returns ONE composited RGBA through the existing STEP_MEDIA adapter. Also noted: a step today sees exactly one media (out.find(m => m.role === step.role), in both _buildStepSlide and _deriveRunMedia), so a place step on image1 cannot see image2 - needs a `sourceRole` on the step declaration, mirroring the existing `mediaRole` that routes a kind's OUTPUT elsewhere. FINDINGS 3-5, all live on Flux.2 Klein 9B, kleinEdit op, 1024x1024 plates. (3) THE STAMP IS A PLACEMENT HINT, NOT A PASTE - a 2D transform cannot RE-PROJECT. A gun photographed from one camera angle cannot be made to sit correctly on a table seen from another by any translate/scale/rotate/stretch; stretching only destroys the object. So the prompt must split GEOMETRY (free: viewing angle, foreshortening, how it rests) from IDENTITY (locked: design, shape, markings, text, colours, materials). Same shape as Draw It In's 'the scribble is where and how big, not an outline the render stays inside'. TWO CONSEQUENCES: a perspective/warp gizmo is DEAD - translate/scale/rotate is enough, which ShapeManager 'place' mode already does; and the stage-2 hint copy is load-bearing, because Fabio spent real effort on 'the best I could do with stamping', i.e. the surface taught him it was a paste. (4) A LONG PROMPT BREAKS IT, AND THE CAUSE IS LICENCE BUDGET, NOT LENGTH. My ~200-word prompt returned a hugely oversized cup. Cause: 'roughly where' + 'approximately the position and size' + an explicit angle freedom + a gravity freedom COMPOUNDED into 'do what you like', and scale went with them. Fabio's single 'rough' in a 13-word prompt costs nothing because nothing competes with it. Root reason the Draw It In prompt can be long and this one cannot: THERE the geometry is enforced mechanically by crop + stitch-back-only-the-box, so the prompt only handles appearance; HERE there is no crop and no mask, so words were asked to enforce geometry, which they are bad at. That is a direct argument for the shipped flow carrying the crop/stitch rather than treating it as optional. (5) THE LOGO CASE PASSES, and it was the predicted-hardest one. Google logo stamped onto a plain mug came back PRINTED ON and correctly wrapped to the cylinder, letterforms intact, with NO surface-conforming clause in the prompt - Klein already knows how to project a graphic onto a curved surface, it only needs telling where. TWO OF MY PREDICTIONS WERE WRONG: the logo did NOT need the stamped composite in slot 1 (clean scene in slot 1 preserved the letterforms fine), and front-loading the proven Draw It In guardrails was backwards - each of those clauses exists because a specific bug appeared, so they must be added ONE AT A TIME on evidence. CURRENT BASELINE PROMPT (Fabio's, works on mug + logo): 'Add image three to image one using image two as a rough reference for location.' Slots: 1 = clean scene, 2 = pixel stamp, 3 = object on no background. Open: the GUN is the only case that needed an angle licence, so the likely shipping instruction is that sentence plus 'Adjust its angle to fit the scene.' - to be tested on the gun plate next.

FINDINGS 6-7, and the prompt has converged. (6) WHY THE SAME PROMPT WON ONE TEST AND LOST THE OTHER - the two tasks differ in whether anything BOUNDS the scale. A logo applied to a mug is bounded by the mug's own face, so extra licence in the prompt has nowhere to go and costs nothing; a cup dropped onto a table is free-standing, nothing bounds it but image two, so the moment the prompt hedged with 'approximately' the scale drifted and returned a giant cup. Same root cause as finding 4 one level up: PROMPTS ARE BAD AT GEOMETRY, and whatever constrains geometry MECHANICALLY makes the wording stop mattering. A surface does it for the logo; a crop would do it for everything. PREDICTION TO BANK: with InpaintCropImproved sized from the placed bbox, a too-large object physically cannot fit the region, so scale is bounded by the graph rather than by an adjective - the longer prompt should therefore stop breaking the free-standing-object case once cropped, giving ONE prompt that serves both. Untested; it can only be tested inside the flow's real graph. No shadow clause, no glow guard, no 'change nothing else', no identity clause - none has been earned by an observed failure yet, and finding 4 says adding them speculatively is what broke scale. FINDINGS 8-11. PROMPT AND REFERENCE CONFIG ARE NOW SETTLED; the gun angle is the only open failure. (8) VENDOR PROMPTING RULES, researched after Fabio challenged that I was inventing prompt craft rather than reading it (he was right). Sources: docs.bfl.ml FLUX.2 image editing, fal.ai Klein prompt guide, deAPI 'Prompting FLUX.2 Klein'. Rules that actually changed the work: (a) PROMPT LENGTH IS A BAND, roughly 40-120 words - fal says over 100 creates confusion, deAPI says under 40 under-drives the Qwen3 encoder. My 200-word prompt was over (this is the measured cause of the giant cup); Fabio's 13-word one was under. Target 60-90. (b) IDENTITY IS FREE FROM THE REFERENCE while the model is COPYING - refs retain 'exact proportions, dial markings and case finish' and the prompt is meant to spend its words on POSITIONING AND LIGHTING only. So 'keep its design and markings' is wasted budget - EXCEPT once you license a redraw, when it must come back. (c) MORE THAN 3 REFERENCE IMAGES CAUSES IDENTITY MIXING - we were at exactly 3 when we got the duplicated gun. (d) numbered image references are the documented pattern (Fabio was right, I had dropped them). (e) content nouns outweigh modifiers, which is why hedges like 'approximately' both fail to constrain AND dilute. (f) below 768px quality drops, optimal 1024-1536 - consistent with cropping then resizing to 1024. CAUTION ON ONE RULE: the guides say negative/prohibitive phrasing is ignored, but MPI-567 MEASURED the opposite on this exact model (asking for a shadow produced a lit dust cloud; forbidding glow cured it). Our measurement wins on our graph; the word-budget argument alone justifies dropping the guards until a glow actually appears. (9) SHIPPING PROMPT, ~75 words, in band, all positive, two references: 'Place the object from image two into the scene of image one, at the position and size it has in image two. Rest it naturally on the surface it touches, at an angle that matches the camera in image one. Light it with the scene's own light, matching direction, colour temperature and contrast, with contact shading where it meets the surface and a shadow consistent with the shadows already in the scene. Keep everything else in image one unchanged.' CONFIG: slot 1 = clean scene, slot 2 = stamped composite. Two refs, not three. This is the first prompt to pass the logo-on-mug AND the free-standing-cup cases together. MY PREDICTION THAT THE CROP WOULD BE WHAT UNIFIED THEM WAS WRONG - getting into the word band and dropping to two references did it with no crop at all. (10) THE GUN ANGLE IS NOT A PROMPT PROBLEM. THE FIRST RUN LOOKED LIKE A SUCCESS AND WAS NOT - no error, a gallery card, 'Generation finished', and an output of ONE SAMPLE (62 microseconds). Root cause: setuptools 83 removed pkg_resources, so resemble-perth's perth.perth_net fails to import and perth.PerthImplicitWatermarker is None - but `import perth` still succeeds, so chatterbox/vc.py sets PERTH_AVAILABLE=True and calls None(). FL_ChatterboxVC catches every exception and returns torch.zeros((1,2,1)) @ 16kHz, then reports success; its `message` output carries the error and our graph does not wire it. Fixed by uninstalling resemble-perth from the engine python - and the engine MUST be restarted after, since PERTH_AVAILABLE is read at import time. The pack's own requirements.txt keeps resemble-perth commented out, so a fresh engine is unaffected; how many existing users carry the leftover is UNKNOWN.
